items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I got Conte Condoli playing with us and his brother

ctx.x: Well you’ve been able to employ some pretty hot sidemen with your own band, in addition to your own arranging, you’ve had some great contributions from people. Don Menza you mentioned—

Don Menza, a marvelous, a great player. He’s borderline genius too, he really is. He’s something else. He’s a great player. Pete Christlieb, another sax player, Ricky Woodard now just joined us, and he’s another great saxophone player. I got Conte Condoli playing with us and his brother, and oh just Carl Fontana works with us now and then, Frank Strazzeri on piano, John Heard on bass. And now I have three bands you know. I have my New York band, a Chicago band and an L.A. band. Because if I get a gig in New York,…
Yeah, sure do. I recently heard the Slide Hampton Big Band in New York and the way they have some adventuresome writing there.

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then later on, when Don passed away, I took over as – leading from the drums, because Pearl’s television show – in 1972 she did 15 shows. That band – the trumpet section was Sweets Edison, Snooky Young, Cat Anderson, Johnny – the guy that . . . – oh, Conte Candoli, and Johnny . . .

ctx.x: So you’re conductor, not drummer? You didn’t do both duties?

Oh yeah. I let Don do the conducting. I let Don do the tempos. I started the tempos off. He was good with it. He knew the tempos too. Then later on, when Don passed away, I took over as – leading from the drums, because Pearl’s television show – in 1972 she did 15 shows. That band – the trumpet section was Sweets Edison, Snooky Young, Cat Anderson, Johnny – the guy that . . . – oh, Conte Candoli, and Johnny . . .

items.title: Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, 1997
items.q: I am rehearsing now with Louie Bellson. He’s doing a big band album next week in L.A.

ctx.x: Something like that. I was working The Lighthouse and I was doing well on the coast, and when that accident happened, Max Roach called me and wanted me to come work with the band. And I couldn’t leave town. I’d just established myself there pretty well, and I couldn’t leave, so I had to turn it down. I don’t know whether I’m sorry I did. As things worked out, they worked out pretty good. You know I just found out something not too long ago. I am rehearsing now with Louie Bellson. He’s doing a big band album next…
